hook.text: Stephin Merritt first aimed for 100 love songs, then settled on 69 split across three volumes.

facts.label: Recorded
facts.value: April 1999, at Polar West, Mother West, Polar Mother and Sonics

sentences.text: Merritt sat in a Manhattan piano bar, a gay one, listening to a pianist play Stephen Sondheim songs.
There he decided to move into theatre music, feeling he had a knack for it.
The first idea was a music revue with four drag queens, and the one the crowd liked best that night would get paid.
He also took inspiration from Charles Ives's 114 Songs, a collection he had read about that same day.
Much of the writing took place at Dick's Bar in New York, and by his own account he spent eight hours a day there.
Merritt also plays a long list of instruments on the record, from ukulele and musical saw to kalimbas and rain stick.
Shirley Simms, LD Beghtol and Dudley Klute add vocals on a number of songs.
In December 2006 Continuum published a book on the album by LD Beghtol, part of its 33 1/3 series.
It includes studio stories, a glossary of words from the lyrics, and an interview with Merritt.
Domino reissued it in the United Kingdom, and Circus released it in Europe and Australia in 2000.
Peter Gabriel covered The Book of Love, and Black Country, New Road covered I Think I Need a New Heart on an EP.
Superchunk covered I Don't Want to Get Over You in 2025.

listen_for.text: Merritt sings this one as a duet, and the lyric tells the story of a husband who murders his wife.
Shirley Simms sings a duet with Merritt on it.

listen_for.track: Time Enough for Rocking When We're Old
listen_for.text: John Woo plays banjo, lead guitar, mandolin and bass on it.
Daniel Handler plays accordion and keyboards on it, and he also arranged it.

listen_for.track: The Luckiest Guy on the Lower East Side
listen_for.text: Ida Pearle plays violin on it, and Dudley Klute sings lead.
